question: What is the number of water of crystallisation molecules present in plaster of Paris?
solution:
The correct answer is __(1)/(2)__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The set quantity of water molecules found in one salt formula unit constitutes the **water of crystallisation.**
 
• CaSO4. (1)/(2)__H2O is the **plaster of Paris's chemical formula.**
 
• As a result,** one plaster of Paris molecule contains (1)/(2) water for crystallisation.**
 
• It is also known as **calcium sulphate hemihydrate** for this reason.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **No water of crystallisation remains at 393 K,** and **anhydrous calcium sulphate**, CaSO₄, is created instead.
 
• This is referred to as** "dead burned plaster."**
 
• Uses
 
 
• **Plaster of Paris **is mostly used in the **building sector**, along with plasters.
 
• **When a bone is broken or sprained, it is used** to immobilise the damaged area of the organ.
 
• Additionally, it is used in dentistry, decorative arts, and the casting of statues and busts.
